arguments.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: v148 authored whole-body medical-aid animation atlas for a modern battlefield game.
Primary request: Generate ONE new PNG containing exactly EIGHT independent full-body cels of the same adult infantryman performing quiet medical-kit handwork in the single posture specified below. This is a new animation, not an edit of a reference or a posture-transition sheet.
Style and identity guidance: Match the detailed realistic painted finish and adult anatomical proportions of the previously viewed olive infantry stance and kneeling/prone reload references: muted olive/khaki fabric uniform, olive tactical helmet, covered vest and utility pouches, gloves, knee protection, and worn dark combat boots. The same unbranded adult soldier throughout, natural human face and joint construction, painted fabric folds and restrained metal highlights. No chunky, blocky, programmatic pixel-character anatomy. Strict side profile facing RIGHT, no three-quarter view or camera rotation.
Actor and props: ONE actor per cel, whole body fully visible. One rifle remains safely and securely slung flat BEHIND his back, untouched, in a physically consistent position throughout. Both hands are available for medical work. One small olive unmarked IFAK medical pouch and one unmarked off-white bandage roll/dressing, with no symbols. The bandage is a small physical fabric object, not an extra limb or weapon.
Layout: Exactly FOUR columns by TWO rows, eight equal invisible square cells, read left-to-right across the top row then left-to-right across the bottom row. Prefer 2048x1024, landscape 2:1. Render the full eight-cel sheet, not a cropped close-up or collage. Genuine transparent RGBA PNG: empty pixels alpha exactly zero. No background color, checkerboard, opaque backdrop, haze, glow, or shadows.
Cell isolation and registration: Intentionally leave generous EMPTY transparent gutters. Fit the ENTIRE figure, slung rifle, boots, pouch, fingers and extended dressing within the central 72% of each cell width, with at least 14% transparent space at each side, and at least 12% clear space above and below. No part touches any neighbor, cell boundary or image border. Choose one compact anatomical body scale and preserve it in ALL eight cels; never enlarge horizontal or prone figures. As a scale guide, this adult's full standing height at this scale would be about 60% of a cell height; kneeling and prone heights are correspondingly lower, never independently enlarged. Preserve the same body anchor/contact center and horizontal position in every cell. All contact points use the same invisible baseline at 84% of each cell height. Pelvis, torso and head height are fixed for the chosen posture; only small, anatomically plausible arm, wrist, finger and bandage movements animate. No body bobbing, scaling, stance drift or camera motion.
Timing: Eight subtly different chronological frames intended as a gentle 2.4-second looping handwork animation. Frame 7 returns close to frame 0's starting handwork, with a small distinct in-between difference, so frame 7 to frame 0 loops smoothly. Do not duplicate all frames or skip the return motion. No timing text.
Avoid: patients, wounded people, blood, additional people, scene, floor, terrain, ground marks, cast shadows, text, captions, numbering, grids, borders, cross icons, logos, raised arms overhead, command gestures, ladders, climbing, running, crawling, pose transitions, extra limbs, missing fingers, missing or multiplying props. Actor only; the invisible ground is just a registration baseline.

POSTURE: STANDING ONLY. Both boots are firmly planted in precisely the same locations throughout all eight cels. Legs remain straight but natural, with identical knee angles, pelvis height and head height. No knee dip, squatting, kneeling, stepping, swaying or leaning down. All handwork stays between waist and lower chest, safely below the shoulders. Fixed calm side-profile head directed slightly toward his hands.
Eight-frame sequence:
0: both hands poised around the closed IFAK at waist level, starting to prepare it.
1: one hand steadies the pouch while the other pinches its opening flap.
2: slowly open the pouch at the same waist position.
3: lift the edge of a small bandage roll just clear of the opening.
4: one hand supports the roll while the other slowly draws out a short off-white bandage strip at waist/lower-chest level.
5: extend the strip slightly farther with a small wrist movement, both arms remaining low.
6: guide the loose strip gently back toward the pouch/roll as the hands draw closer.
7: hands ease back around the pouch to nearly the starting preparation position for the repeat; retain a tiny hand-position difference from frame 0.
The standing whole-body silhouette and slung rifle remain stable throughout. Render exactly this single eight-frame standing medical-aid atlas.

caveats: All originals are 1774x887 RGBA, not the preferred 2048x1024; nominal grid divisions therefore fall on half pixels.
Standing figures have only about 10-15 pixels of top/bottom cell clearance.
Kneeling forward reach comes within about 13 pixels of a cell boundary; generous margins were not fully followed.
Prone silhouettes occupy roughly 90-94% of cell width, leaving as little as 3 pixels side clearance at alpha >16.
Prone contact baselines differ by roughly 15-16 pixels between the two rows; some torso, elbow and head movement remains.
Anatomical scale is not matched across the three separate posture sheets, especially the larger kneeling actor.
Exact pose registration and smoothness of the intended 2.4-second loop need parent runtime review.
